slices.name: ws01-32-a11y-sweep-close-out
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 32 of 32, the last one (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD c52848e02ee4dab596c4a5cb65289a69c78328f4 (slice 31's own commit); the base for diffs is c52848e02ee4dab596c4a5cb65289a69c78328f4. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. Checkpoint D (PR 108) merges to main after this slice, with a merge-safety review by someone who has not followed the work, so what this slice records must let that reviewer work from REDESIGN_STATUS.md alone. The lead's notes on the browser harness (give each browser-test server its own database; make the baseline sampler, the hero-ring test and the arrow-key test wait for their data and retry once) are done: they landed as commit abe7d07 before slice 30, slices 30 and 31 changed none of test/a11y/global-setup.ts, support.ts or baseline.ts, and this slice leaves test/a11y/global-setup.ts, baseline.ts, baseline.json and the helpers in test/a11y/support.ts alone, opening every page through openDrawn. Every line number below was measured on the working tree that held slice 31 finished and not yet committed, the tree this slice starts from; slice 31's commit is expected to hold exactly those files, but read any file before you edit it and do not trust a cited line without looking at it. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (1,926 lines on the starting tree): the Ordering rules (lines 7 to 11); the WS01 header (lines 13 to 17: Status 15, Branch 16, PR 17); the acceptance table (lines 21 to 58): the paragraph above it (21), the AC1 row (25), the only row still Planned and this slice's, the AC7 row (31), whose second half is K's lab run on a preview, the AC9 row (33), whose live half is K's and stays 'not done yet', the AC10 to AC13 rows (34 to 37) as the pattern for a filled row, the K1d row (42), the K5 row (55) and the T1 row (57, whose text says 'Dark, live and heritage on every page are AC1's, step 32'); the step 31 block (lines 876 to 918) in full, above all its Files (880), The switches (891), The places left for later (897), Judgement calls (898 to 914), Lint (915), Build (916), The browser runs (917, with its accessibility pass on three heritage pages and its dark spot run) and Checks (918), with the step 30 block (837 to 874) and the step 29 block (804 to 835) as the pattern for a step block, and the Checkpoint C section (497 to 512) and the Checkpoint B section (335 on) as the pattern for a section that faces a merge; Decisions (heading at line 920): the five step 31 lines, 1015 to 1019, which this slice leaves word for word, and 'Contracts are a ratchet' (927), 'Dark mode' (931), 'Checkpoints' (944), the step 20 Decision on the known violations (972), 'The scope switches need newLook (step 21)' (976) and 'Dark mode and the Appearance control (step 21)' (978); Deviations (heading at line 1021): the one planned line for this step, 'AC1's live and heritage runs (step 32)', line 1142, which this slice keeps word for word and marks done, with 'AC13 compares screenshots from the same run (step 31)', line 1141, as the pattern for a planned line marked done, and the Step 31 entry, lines 1325 to 1335, as the pattern for a deviation entry, with its sub-bullet on the spec's test file name (1333) and its sub-bullet 'Files beyond the step's list:' (1335); Verify items (heading at line 1337): the step 31 ones, lines 1593 to 1613, as the pattern, above all 'The date line (step 31)' (1611), 'Lint and counts (step 31)' (1612) and 'The baseline (step 31)' (1613); Follow-ups (heading at line 1615): the entries that hand work to this step, which are, by line, 1703 (the hero carousel and the known-violations list, step 20), 1704 (the muted status pill, step 20), 1713 (dark, live and heritage under the checker, step 21), 1722 (classes only documents and tests name reach the stylesheet, step 23), 1723 (selected navy controls in dark mode, step 23), 1724 (gold grounds in dark mode, step 23), 1726 (navy text on the tournament hero's gold tint, step 23; older than the step), 1731 (the filter menu clips its options' ring, step 23), 1745 (the State champions link, step 25; older than the step), 1746 (gold that is not text, step 25), 1765 (the baseline sampler waits for content, step 27), 1776 (image files nothing uses, step 28; older than the step), 1782 (the news band's picture with no width or height, step 29; older than the step) and 1793 (the layout shift as measured, step 31, whose last sentence hands the site's loading-line budget to WS02 or to this step); and the older entries the manifest's list names, 'AC9 live check' (1617), 'Enforcement at checkout (step 15)' (1633), 'Contracts as endpoints change (step 7)' (1658), 'Games by name' (1663), 'Schedules in WS06 and WS08 (step 14)' (1674), 'Retiring the JSON columns' (1675), 'tournament_games.section_id (WS07)' (1676), 'Remove test.fixme (step 20)' (1707), 'ScrollPanel on the long screens (step 26)' (1753), 'The email preview's logo file (step 28; older than the step)' (1771) and 'K's lab run on the preview (step 29)' (1779); the step 31 follow-ups, 1792 to 1799, with 'K reviews the step 31 judgement calls (step 31)' (1792) as the pattern for a K-reviews follow-up; docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (acceptance criterion 1, line 348; the test list, lines 363 to 372, whose bullet at line 369 names test/a11y/scopes.spec.ts; the WS01 deviations list, line 112, which ends with the step 31 sentence), docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md (line 156, what WS01 grows by; line 607, the same acceptance criterion; line 617, the same spec); src/App.tsx (all 159 lines: the layout's lazy import 55 to 56; the six heritage routes written once in HERITAGE_PAGES, 63 to 72; the site's main, 80; the Suspense, 81 to 92; the routes, 95 to 151, with the nine AC1 routes at 95 (/), 96 (/tournaments), 97 (/tournaments/:id), 100 (/scholastic), 101 (/clubs), 109 (/membership), and in HERITAGE_PAGES 66 (/about), 68 (/champions) and 70 (/governance/minutes); the choice of layout, 119; the fixture route, 149 to 151), src/layouts/HeritageLayout.tsx (the real scope: a div marked data-layout="heritage" inside the site's main), src/lib/features.ts (newLook 44, themeHeritage 53, themeScholastic 60, FEATURES 197), src/lib/colorScheme.ts (how .dark reaches the page), src/pages/TournamentsPage.tsx (line 531, the State champions link), src/pages/TournamentDetailPage.tsx (lines 578 to 586, the "See pairings / results" button, its class at line 580), the other places the follow-ups name (src/pages/ClubsPage.tsx 126, src/pages/ScannerPage.tsx 869, src/areas/events/components/MiniCalendar.tsx 77, src/components/FilterDropdown.tsx 67, src/components/MultiSelectDropdown.tsx 79, src/components/ImpersonationBanner.tsx 9, src/components/AnnouncementBanner.tsx 14, the news band's component under src/components, line 212), src/index.css (the base look, lines 395 to 415 and its dark block 457; the live look 502, which sets color-scheme: dark, so it is a dark look on every device; scholastic 551; heritage 603 and its dark block 620; the rule that gives heritage's controls the base tokens, 646 to 690; the rules on every scope, 705 and 757; the focus ring), src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx (FIXTURE_SCOPES at 31, its one ThemeScope at 84), scripts/seed/fixtures.sql (the four tournaments, lines 89, 106, 124 and 132), and the tests: test/a11y/smoke.spec.ts (all 86 lines), test/a11y/known-violations.json (all of it), test/a11y/dark-spot.spec.ts (all 117 lines), test/a11y/chess-data.spec.ts (93 to 128 and 245 to 300), test/a11y/components.spec.ts (40 to 130), test/a11y/components-edges.spec.ts (335 to 360), test/a11y/brand.spec.ts (296 to 372), test/a11y/brand-edges.spec.ts (280 to 336), test/a11y/home.spec.ts (295 to 310), test/a11y/heritage.spec.ts (its header comment, lines 1 to 75, and the accessibility pass at 776 to 803), test/a11y/support.ts (DRAWN_TIMEOUT 97, openDrawn 110, the external fixture 85 to 94), test/a11y/global-setup.ts (66 to 77, the two builds' switches), playwright.config.ts, test/a11y/baseline.ts and baseline.json (to leave alone), test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (418 to 452, the pins on the known-violations list, and 455 to 490, the list of browser-test files checked for dashes and tool names), test/unit/gold-icons-words.test.ts (107 to 117, the pin on the State champions link), test/unit/contracts-status.test.ts (25 to 27, the K1d row), test/unit/preview-database.test.ts (208 to 246, the table's rows, AC9 and the AC9 follow-up), test/unit/redesign-status-step23.test.ts (207 to 212, the WS01 header), test/unit/redesign-status-step29.test.ts (329 to 345, the hero carousel entry), test/unit/features.test.ts, and test/unit/redesign-status-step30.test.ts and redesign-status-step31.test.ts (all of both, so the step 32 records leave their expectations true). The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and the harness notes, which are done): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 32) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. node_modules is installed, the accessibility checker's package included, and nothing in it is changed by this slice; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy. Georgia is not installed in this container, so a browser test here draws the device's serif wherever a look names a face that is not loaded; none of this slice's checks depends on a face. This slice expects to add no dependency; a package is allowed only as an exact-pinned development dependency (no caret) published on or before 2026-10-08 (today is 2026-10-22, so two weeks old), with package-lock.json updated by npm install through the proxy, and the record says so. If an install fails, say so with the error and stop that part: do not vendor files, loosen a pin or disable TLS checks. The branch tip is c52848e02ee4dab596c4a5cb65289a69c78328f4 and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries later commits only once the lead pushes, and the local main ref does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against c52848e02ee4dab596c4a5cb65289a69c78328f4, and checkpoint D's as the working tree against a25c4a5 (the commit that recorded the checkpoint C merge). A full test:a11y run starts servers on ports 8801 and 8802 (each over a database of its own; read test/a11y/global-setup.ts for where), so never run two of them at once, and never run one while a build is running.

Build exactly this. Run AC1 and close out WS01. Merge checkpoint D follows (sub-PR 4 = slices 20 to 32). test/a11y/scopes.spec.ts (new) is the full matrix. It covers /, /tournaments, the seeded tournament detail page, /clubs, /membership, /scholastic, /about, /governance/minutes and /champions, each in four modes on the a11y-on build: light; dark (.dark on the html element); live and heritage (data-theme set on the page's content element through page.evaluate, so every page's real content is tested under each token set). It also covers the scholastic fixture page. The accessibility checker's Playwright package runs with the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa (the AXE_TAGS list every browser spec already carries). The spec fails on any serious or critical violation and prints the rule, selector, page and mode. Fix every violation inside WS01's scope: tokens under data-look=new first, shared components second, then the page class that causes it. Every fix is token-level or gated on data-look=new or a flag, so the a11y-off baseline stays unchanged; an ungated fix is allowed only when it changes nothing visible (an accessible name, a heading level, a scope attribute) and is listed. There is no nav or homepage redesign here; anything bigger is recorded as a follow-up for the owning workstream. Run the whole browser suite green (smoke, tokens, scope-switch, components, chess-data, brand, home, heritage, scopes, and every other spec under test/a11y). Update REDESIGN_STATUS.md: each of AC1 to AC14 and K1a to K6 with the slice and test that proves it (K1d as K answered); deviations, verify items, and every flag with what K should look at on the preview; and the follow-ups: retiring the tournaments.sections and round_schedule JSON columns and the 0053 sync trigger; tournament_games.section_id; per-section cap enforcement, holds, the schedule picker and the family member limit in WS06; the contracts-pending count; pages to thin in WS05, WS06 and WS08, with ScrollPanel applied to long screens such as tournament setup; the AdminEmailPage logo; the AC9 live check; the e2e specs once WS06 and WS07 exist. Write the PR text in plain language, with no AI references, no attribution lines, no internal workflow terms and no em dashes. The differences below say how each of these meets the tree; where this brief and the manifest differ, this brief wins.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): AC1 page list against routes. (All nine routes exist in App.tsx (/, /tournaments, /tournaments/:id, /clubs, /membership, /scholastic, /about, /governance/minutes, /champions); the detail page uses the tournament seeded by scripts/seed/fixtures.sql. Re-checked: it holds in part. The nine routes exist at the lines given above, three of them (/about, /governance/minutes, /champions) written in HERITAGE_PAGES and drawn inside the layout when themeHeritage is on (difference 1). The seed holds four tournaments, not one: fx-t-open (upcoming, registration open, three sections, line 89), fx-t-quads (upcoming, run by a club, 106), fx-t-legacy (upcoming, a draft whose sections are plain strings, 124) and fx-t-done (completed, with entries, games and half-point results, 132); only a tournament with published pairings shows the live "See pairings / results" button (difference 5). The App.tsx holds 35 page routes in all (the nine, 14 other public ones, the heritage Annual meeting, Board and Bylaws pages, and 9 protected ones), 3 redirects and the a11y-only fixture route; AC1 names the nine, and the 26 others are recorded as not covered by it.) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the tree this slice starts from (slice 31 finished). (1) Three of the nine routes are in a real heritage scope on a11y-on, so a data-theme on main does not reach them. With themeHeritage on, src/App.tsx (line 119) holds /about, /governance/minutes and /champions, with the other three heritage routes, inside HeritageLayout, which draws them in ThemeScope scope="heritage" as a div marked data-layout="heritage" inside the site's one main (src/layouts/HeritageLayout.tsx, line 69). So on a11y-on those three pages are already heritage in light and in dark, and an attribute set on main is shadowed for everything inside that div. The manifest's way (data-theme on main through page.evaluate) therefore reads the six routes the layout does not draw: /, /tournaments, the detail page, /clubs, /membership and /scholastic. For the three, set the attribute on the scope div: "" gives the base look (test/a11y/brand-edges.spec.ts line 288 does exactly this), "live" gives live, and the page as drawn is heritage. Say in the record what each mode means for each page (light and dark are the base look on a light and a dark device, which for the three needs the scope div set to ""; heritage is the page as drawn for the three and an attribute for the six), and why. The ground has to be painted as a box scope paints it (asLiveScope in test/a11y/chess-data.spec.ts, lines 112 to 118, adds bg-background and text-foreground to main), with the header and the footer left in the base look. A look's type and stylesheet are requested by ThemeScope's own effect, which a hand-set attribute never runs, so the matrix reads the looks' colours and not their type, as the live readings in chess-data.spec.ts do; say so. ThemeScope's nesting check works on the component tree and never sees a hand-set attribute, so heritage inside heritage is not reported. The live look is a dark look on any device (src/index.css line 502 sets color-scheme: dark), so one device reading of it is enough; heritage has a dark block (line 620), so it is read on a light and a dark device. The planned line at 1142 says the runs "set the look on each page's main": keep it word for word and mark it done with what was really done. (2) What the checker runs on today, so the matrix adds to it and moves nothing. test/a11y/smoke.spec.ts runs it on / alone, in the light look, on both builds, and fails on any finding the known list does not name. test/a11y/dark-spot.spec.ts runs it on /, /tournaments and /membership in dark mode on a11y-on, and fails only on a colour-contrast finding whose text is navy or whose ground is white or is not explained; every other finding is printed (line 98 to 104) and never asserted, so its output "1 other rule(s) with findings" on /tournaments is an open finding (difference 5). test/a11y/heritage.spec.ts (776 to 803) runs it on /about, /governance/minutes and /champions, light and dark, at 1280 and 390 pixels, and finds nothing. test/a11y/brand.spec.ts and brand-edges.spec.ts run it on /about and on the header and footer at 1280 and 390, light and dark. test/a11y/components.spec.ts and components-edges.spec.ts run it inside the four fixture containers (at 1280 pixels in light and in dark, at 390 in light). test/a11y/chess-data.spec.ts runs it on main of the pairings and print pages of fx-t-done in the base look and as a live scope (245 to 300). test/a11y/home.spec.ts runs it on the still hero. No spec runs it on /tournaments in the light look, on the detail page, /clubs, /scholastic, or /membership in the light look. (3) AC1 asks for zero serious or critical findings; every other spec in the suite fails on a finding of any impact. Keep the suite's habit for the WCAG-tagged rules (a failure on any finding, with the rule, impact, selector, page, mode and, for colour, the two colours and the ratio printed), and say it in the record as a judgement call: the floor AC1 sets is met either way, and a moderate finding under the WCAG tags is rare. Print the checker's "incomplete" colour-contrast results (a hero's words over a picture are one) with their selectors, without failing, and record each as reviewed or as a follow-up; a pass count alone does not prove AC1. Collect every cell's findings before the first assertion, so a first run prints the whole list and a fix is not found one cell at a time. (4) The known-violations list cannot be emptied the way the manifest and the step 20 decision say, and the manifest's own rule is why. test/a11y/known-violations.json holds 18 entries, nine for each build, all on / : three colour-contrast lines (".gap-2.text-sm.flex > .text-muted-foreground" and the two muted lines in the upcoming-events and clubs lists) and six target-size entries for the hero slideshow's dots (".w-5" and "Slide 1" to "Slide 5"). On a11y-on none is found any more (the new look's tokens clear the three muted lines, and step 29 took the dots out under newLook), so smoke.spec.ts reports all nine as listed but not found; on a11y-off eight of the nine were found at step 29 (the dot the slideshow is on moves, so one dot's entry is not found on a given run). The a11y-off entries are today's site with every switch off: the muted lines are today's grey and the dots are today's slideshow, so fixing them changes what a visitor sees with the switches off, which the manifest forbids outside the cases it names, and which test/a11y/baseline.json would then be compared against; the follow-up at line 1781 gives the dots to WS03, which deletes the slideshow. The tree also pins the list: test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (418 to 452) requires the list to be non-empty, its comment to say "step 32" and "nothing new may be added", every route to be "/", the two builds to list the same findings and smoke.spec.ts to name no disabled rule, and test/unit/redesign-status-step29.test.ts (329 to 345) holds the carousel entry (line 1703) to a "Step 29:" sentence and no "Done in step 29". So measure first: run the matrix and smoke.spec.ts on both builds, and for each of the 18 entries say whether it is found, on which build and why. Then choose and record, with every pin you move listed: the a11y-off entries stay, with the reason (today's look, WS03 for the dots, newLook for the greys), and the sweep is proved on a11y-on, where the same three muted lines and the dots no longer fail; or, only if you find a fix that is gated on newLook or changes nothing visible on a11y-off, that fix. The nine a11y-on entries may go, but only together with the pin that the two builds list the same findings, moved with its reason; you may also leave them. Nothing is added to the file. Leave the Decision at line 972 word for word and put the outcome in the AC1 row, the Step 32 deviation and the follow-up at line 1703 (a "Step 32:" sentence, and "Done in step 32" only if the file really is emptied). The K5 row (55) and the step 20 verify items say "step 32 empties the list"; correct that with a Step 32 sentence, not by rewriting them. (5) Findings the records already hold that no spec fails on, which the matrix will meet. (a) The State champions link on /tournaments (src/pages/TournamentsPage.tsx line 531, gold on the navy hero, 6.51:1) is set apart from the white words around it by its colour alone until it is hovered, which the checker reports as link-in-text-block in both looks (follow-up at 1745; dark-spot.spec.ts prints it without failing). It needs a mark that is not colour; an underline changes what a visitor sees with the switches off, so draw it under newLook only (a rule under :root[data-look="new"], or a class that waits for it), and move test/unit/gold-icons-words.test.ts (107 to 117), which holds that exact line. (b) "See pairings / results" on a tournament that has games (src/pages/TournamentDetailPage.tsx line 580, class text-ink on a 15 per cent gold tint over the navy hero) is navy words on navy, about 1.3:1 (follow-up at 1726, which says the light look needs light words there; no spec has run the checker on this page); expect a colour-contrast finding on fx-t-done in the light look, and fix it under newLook with words that read on the hero in both devices. (c) Anything else the first run finds on /clubs, /scholastic, /membership and /tournaments in the light look, which nothing has measured. The manifest's risk stands: the count is unknown until the matrix runs, and a fix larger than a token, a shared component or one page class becomes a follow-up for the owning workstream rather than a redesign. (6) The fixtures. The scholastic fixture page is /__fixtures/scholastic (src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx draws ThemeScope scope="scholastic" itself, line 84, whatever themeScholastic says; both browser-test builds leave themeScholastic off, so /scholastic never wears the scholastic look in a browser test). The existing runs (components.spec.ts, components-edges.spec.ts) include only the fixture container; the sweep runs the whole fixture page, light and dark, at both widths, and says what the page's own chrome adds. The muted pair (the closed status pill, #737373 on #f5f5f5, 4.34:1) is kept out of the a11y-off fixture runs with its reason (components.spec.ts line 98 holds it to exactly that finding) and reads 5.58:1 under newLook; the follow-up at 1704 hands it to this step, but the a11y-off pair is today's look, so it stays (the same reasoning as difference 4) and the answer is a Step 32 sentence there. (7) Dark. src/lib/colorScheme.ts puts .dark on html itself from the device setting (and the Appearance control), as dark-spot.spec.ts lines 51 and 66 show (colorScheme: 'dark' on the page, html.dark and data-look "new" true, the body rgb(11, 18, 32)); the matrix emulates the device rather than adding the class by hand, and asserts the class. (8) The harness is done (abe7d07): see the opening. A new spec uses openDrawn with locators for the page's heading and the data it shows (rows, cards, lists), skips by testInfo.project.name as brand.spec.ts does, asserts the external list is empty and that the page raised no script error. Playwright's retries are 0, test timeout 60 seconds, and .github/workflows/ci.yml now runs npm run test:a11y as a job of its own on pull requests, so the new spec runs in PR 108's own checks: it must not depend on timing, on the order of tests, or on the hero's pictures having loaded. (9) The pins that move with this slice. test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (455 to 490) gains test/a11y/scopes.spec.ts in its list of files checked for dashes, tool names and 'AI', so scopes.spec.ts holds none, and its counts follow; the known-violations pins (418 to 452) move only as difference 4 says. test/unit/redesign-status-step31.test.ts keeps its expectations true: the date line pattern allows steps 32 to 39 in front of step 31 (line 105), the first 400 characters must hold steps 18, 21, 23, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30 and 31, exactly 164 follow-ups are headed before step 31 (headings with (step 31) to (step 39) do not count), exactly 6 follow-ups say Done in step 31, one Done in step 30, one Done in step 29, one Done in step 28 and none Done in step 27, exactly five Decisions lines contain (step 31), and the planned AC13 line keeps its words. test/unit/redesign-status-step23.test.ts (207 to 212) holds the WS01 header to the words 'draft pull request 108' and to no 'not pushed yet' and no '**PR:** none yet'. test/unit/contracts-status.test.ts (25 to 27) holds the K1d row to '| 7 | **Partial: ratchet.**' and to '110 lines, count pinned', and test/unit/preview-database.test.ts (208 to 246) holds every row to a step from 1 to 32 and a non-empty proof, the K1d proof to 'partial: ratchet', the AC9 row to step 1, 'test/unit/wrangler-config.test.ts', 'live half' and 'not done yet', and the AC9 follow-up (line 1617) to 'AC9 live check ... first push ... Record the result here'. So "K1d as K answered" is a sentence added after the pinned start of the row, naming K's October 8 decision (Decisions line 927, the lead's note 1: the ratchet, as planned), not a rewrite; AC9 and the AC7 second half stay pending K actions, recorded as such with what K does and where. (10) The table and the records the manifest asks for. Of the 32 rows only AC1 is still Planned (K1d is Partial by decision, AC9 half done, AC7 half done); this slice fills AC1 in the pattern of AC10 to AC13 (what proves it, the test files, the numbers, the build, the cells run, what was found and fixed, what stays and why) and checks the whole table by a script that the new record test also runs: 32 rows, none containing 'Planned', each with a step and a proof. Of the manifest's eight follow-ups, entries already exist for the JSON columns and the 0053 triggers (1675), tournament_games.section_id (1676 and 1663), the schedule picker (1674), the contracts count (1658), ScrollPanel on long screens (1753), the email preview's logo (1771), the AC9 live check (1617) and the e2e specs (1707); a grep for per-section cap enforcement, holds and the family member limit finds no entry, and the thin pages are a Decision (966) and a step 19 line (492) and not a follow-up. For each of the eight, add a follow-up headed (step 32) only where no entry says it, name the owning workstream, and otherwise add a Step 32 sentence to the entry or leave it; never rename or remove an entry (tests from step 23 to step 31 pin headings and counts).
